# OCV reconfiguration across a collapse and a rebuild — Haltern vs. KDLO, two verdicts

*generated by `code/sds/ocv_reconfigure.py`; the design is fixed in `code/sds/ocv_reconfigure_spec.md`, including the 2026-10-22 amendment that separates the two assets and amendment 5 that registers this pair*

Each asset is measured against **its own reference state**, in units of that reference's own variability — Haltern against `pre-collapse (healthy)` on the support-sized chip, with the post-collapse state as the single contrast, KDLO against `pre` on the support-sized chip, with the rebuilt state as the single contrast and one orbit direction only. Assets share a metric, not a scale, so their magnitudes are never compared. Each carries its **own** Holm family — two cells per channel, so four for Haltern and two for KDLO — and its own verdict; no joint label is issued, and the comparison section is a description, not a hypothesis.

## There is no dose

Both assets have exactly two states, separated by the collapse date — Haltern's turbine came down on 2021-09-29, and KDLO's mast collapsed between 2022-12-11 and 2022-12-23 and was rebuilt afterwards (its second state is a *rebuild*, not a ruin), so there is no ladder to order and no frequency drop to regress against. The ordered test reduces to its two-group case — one one-sided rank test between the reference and the other state per block and per asset — and `ΔR` is the step.

| experiment | state | n ASC | n DESC |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Haltern | pre-collapse (healthy) (reference) | 44 | 52 |
| Haltern | post-collapse | 5 | 6 |
| KDLO | pre (reference) | – | 16 |
| KDLO | rebuild | – | 43 |

A `–` is a channel the record does not contain, not a cell that came out empty: KDLO was never acquired ASCENDING. Such a channel carries no cell, no test and no panel, and it contributes nothing to the asset's Holm family.

LUMO's measured frequency ladder is not used here — not by either asset; it is kept under `dose` in the JSON, flagged `applies: false`, and quoted in `data/sds/ocv_reconfigure.md` where it is the dose.

Its own interval still covers a top-step change of up to 3.1 R-units, so what the asset **excludes** for this block is bounded by that number, and nothing smaller.


Haltern has two states and no control track: the turbine came down on 2021-09-29, and `pre-collapse (healthy)` and `post-collapse` are separated by that date alone, so this is a before/after contrast in time, not a controlled comparison. The table is the support-sized chip of the turbine mast (107 of the 120 committed overpasses). The post-collapse state holds 5 ASC and 6 DESC units against 44 ASC and 52 DESC pre-collapse ones; ASC sits below the six-unit threshold the table calls `thin`. No contrast survives the asset's own family, so the intervals above are what these data give.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |

**Verdict — KDLO, behaviour**: the pre-to-rebuild contrast in the behaviour block survives the asset's own Holm family on DESC. Its own interval still covers a top-step change of up to 5.4 R-units, so what the asset **excludes** for this block is bounded by that number, and nothing smaller.

**Verdict — KDLO, geometry**: the pre-to-rebuild contrast in the geometry block survives the asset's own Holm family on DESC. Its own interval still covers a top-step change of up to 65 R-units, so what the asset **excludes** for this block is bounded by that number, and nothing smaller.


KDLO has two states and no control track either: the mast collapsed between 2022-12-11 and 2022-12-23 and was rebuilt, so `pre` and `rebuild` are separated by that event alone — a before/after contrast in time in which the second state is a *new* structure, not a damaged one. The table is the support-sized chip, which here is the whole record (60 acquisitions), and the record carries no ASCENDING acquisition, so this asset has one channel, two H1 cells per block and a two-test Holm family. The reference holds 16 DESC units and the rebuilt state 43 DESC units. The one acquisition in state `single` is excluded before any statistic — the collapse itself, 2022-12-23, and one date cannot carry a median — and counted in the audit, so neither state inherits it. The geometry magnitude of the rebuilt state (`R` = 21.6) is carried by `S` (z = -43.1, 99.6 % of the block's squared magnitude): the reference's `S` median is 22.9 (on the `identity` scale) with a MAD of 0.37, the rebuilt state's is 7.16, and the other three dimensions stay within 2.7 z. `R` is an RMS over four dimensions, so one coordinate can carry it — which is why `S` is annotated beside the plane and not drawn on it.

## Comparison — the same metric, two assets (descriptive)

Not a hypothesis and not a test: the cosine of the two standardised response vectors at the largest state says whether the *same metric*, applied twice to two assets, answers with the same direction. Magnitudes are not compared — each asset's `R` lives on its own scale.

| channel | block | cosine | 95 % CI | sign agreement | null p | Haltern | KDLO |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| DESC | `behaviour` [gamma2, P] | 0.0608 | [-0.96, 0.791] | 1/2 | 0.960 | gamma2+ P- | gamma2- P- |
| DESC | `geometry` [A, D, F, S] | 0.147 | [-0.974, 0.357] | 3/4 | 0.817 | A+ D+ F+ S- | A+ D- F+ S- |

`null p` is the share of random directions in 3 (or 2) dimensions whose absolute cosine is at least as large — a guard against a coarse direction space, not a significance claim. γ² is the same exported quantity in the two chips but measured on different structures at different dates, which is why the two dimensions of the behaviour block are also printed one by one (`z` per asset). The geometry block carries four dimensions while its plane shows two: `R_geometry` is the RMS over `A, D, F, S`, and `D` (which partly inherits `A`) and `S` (position, not morphology) are annotated beside the plane rather than drawn as axes.

### Two verdicts, read together

* **Haltern** — ASC behaviour `R` = 0.819, Holm 1.000; ASC geometry `R` = 0.99, Holm 0.729; DESC behaviour `R` = 0.53, Holm 1.000; DESC geometry `R` = 1.18, Holm 0.729. Resolves no cell at Holm < 0.05.
* **KDLO** — DESC behaviour `R` = 1.68, Holm 0.007; DESC geometry `R` = 21.6, Holm < 0.001. Resolves DESC behaviour, DESC geometry at Holm < 0.05.

None of the 2 cells shares a direction: in every one the cosine is not positive or the signs disagree in at least one dimension. The closest is DESC geometry, cosine 0.147 [-0.974, 0.357] with 3/4 signs equal (null p 0.817) — a cosine that does not carry the block's dimensions with it.

So the comparison does not say that the two towers reorganised alike. It says that one of them reorganised measurably and the other did not, and that no cell has both a positive cosine and agreeing signs — the second asset holds 43 overpasses after the event against 16 before it. That is the answer these data support, and it is not the same as *no change*.

| Haltern | 107 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

A unit is dropped for one dimension only when the transformed value is undefined. Neither tower table loses a unit for any dimension, so every `R` above is computed on the full cell.

**Excluded before any statistic:** KDLO `single` — 1 acquisition: the collapse itself, 2022-12-23, and one date cannot carry a median; counted here and in the JSON audit and never folded into a neighbouring state.

## What this does not claim

* No magnitude comparison between the assets: `R` is scaled by each reference's own variation — and, where the reference is smaller than ten units, by that asset's pooled variation — so the numbers live on different units by construction.
* No joint verdict. Each asset's Holm family, and therefore each asset's verdict and bound, is its own.
* No severity derived from an OCV response: neither tower has an ordered state ladder — the two states are one binary event, and `ΔR` is its size, not a dose response.
* No failure case enters the construction of this metric; projecting them afterwards is a separate step with these definitions frozen.

* **One section of one mast, no control.** The support-sized chip is the `turbine-mast-section` of a single AV9 turbine and the table carries no control track, so the post-collapse signature is confounded with the calendar — unlike Bautzen, whose bridge-minus-control difference removes what the two tracks share.
* **A thin post-collapse cell.** It holds 5 ASC and 6 DESC units against 44 ASC and 52 DESC pre-collapse ones; ASC sits below the six-unit threshold the `Support` column calls `thin`. With this many post-collapse overpasses a null is a statement about what the data can resolve, not about the structure.
* **`gamma2_mask`, not `gamma2_export`.** The behaviour block uses the masked coherence the window rule defines; the asset-point export the same table carries is a single point of the scene, not the site's masked coherence, and is not used.
* **No ordering claim.** `pre` and `post` are one binary event, so only the two-group version of the ordered test is reported.
* **A rebuild, not a ruin.** KDLO's second state is the mast as rebuilt, not the mast as collapsed, so a response there is the difference between two structures — the standing one and its replacement — and not a damage state. Nothing here reads severity off the size of `ΔR`.
* **One channel, half the tests.** The record carries no ASCENDING acquisition, so every cell is a DESC cell: two H1 tests for the asset instead of four, and two cosine cells instead of four. The missing channel is declared in the JSON (`channels_absent`) and drawn as an empty panel; it is never a null.
* **One acquisition excluded, and counted.** `single` — 1 acquisition (the collapse itself, 2022-12-23, and one date cannot carry a median).
* **Support chip = whole record.** All 60 acquisitions of the record lie inside the support, so this table is the record rather than a window on it — the opposite of Haltern's 107 of 120, and the reason the two counts are printed rather than compared.
* **One metric, two events.** The two towers fail for different reasons on different dates with different structures, and only one of them was rebuilt; the shared element is the measurement and the window rule, not the event. A shared cosine direction is not a transfer claim, and no magnitude crosses between the two.
* **Same window rule, verified once.** Both chips were masked by the same rule (`30 %` of the peak and `5 ×` the ring median, 200 m ring, 30 m guard) in `erlking_mvp/tools/ocv_table.py`, the same rule the two bridges were cut with; the comparison inherits that rule rather than re-deriving it.
